definition: Janyce Marbury Wiebe (1959–2018) was an American computer science specializing in natural language processing and known for her work on subjectivity, sentiment analysis, opinion mining, discourse processing, and word-sense disambiguation.

explainer.lead: Janyce Marbury Wiebe (1959–2018) was an American computer scientist specializing in natural language processing, known for work on subjectivity, sentiment analysis, opinion mining, discourse processing, and word-sense disambiguation. Her work matters because it shaped how machines are made to detect opinions and subjective language in text.

tiers.eli5: She was a researcher who taught computers to notice when people are expressing an opinion or feeling rather than just stating a fact.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers building sentiment and opinion-mining systems draw on the framing of subjectivity she established. The pitfall is collapsing her separate topics—subjectivity, sentiment, opinion mining, discourse, word-sense disambiguation—into one problem, when they address different levels of language analysis.
tiers.paperLevel: Her published record covers natural language processing with emphasis on subjectivity, sentiment analysis, opinion mining, discourse processing, and word-sense disambiguation. Known limits: the record gives no formulas or benchmark figures, only the topic areas of her contribution.

explainer.example: A sentiment analysis team cites her subjectivity work when distinguishing sentences that state facts from sentences that express an opinion.
